1	// Package review — see env.go for package-level rationale.
2	//
3	// tui_sink.go provides TUISink, a Sink implementation that renders a Bubble
4	// Tea status dashboard during a review run and supports Ctrl+O
5	// drill-in mode for inspecting one agent's live event buffer. Used in
6	// interactive (TTY) runs; non-TTY runs use DumpSink instead.
7	package review
8	
9	import (
10		"context"
11		"io"
12		"sync"
13		"time"
14	
15		tea "charm.land/bubbletea/v2"
16		"golang.org/x/term"
17	
18		reviewtypes "github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/review/types"
19	)
20	
21	// teaRunner is the slice of *tea.Program the sink depends on, extracted so
22	// tests can substitute a program with a deterministically stalled event loop.
23	type teaRunner interface {
24		Run() (tea.Model, error)
25		Send(msg tea.Msg)
26		Kill()
27	}
28	
29	// tuiSinkQueueCap bounds the sink's internal dispatch queue. Program.Send is
30	// an unbuffered BLOCKING send: if the Bubble Tea Update/render pipeline ever
31	// stalls, a direct Send from the orchestrator's dispatch goroutine parks
32	// forever — freezing sink dispatch, the fanIn drain loop, the parsers, and
33	// reviewer-timeout handling with it (observed live: the 2026-07-07 run-6
34	// wedge, where the TUI froze mid-run and a 20m --timeout never surfaced).
35	// The queue absorbs bursts; overflow beyond the cap is dropped and counted —
36	// a display that can lag must never backpressure the data plane.
37	const tuiSinkQueueCap = 4096
38	
39	// TUISink is a Sink that renders a Bubble Tea dashboard. The orchestrator
40	// calls AgentEvent/RunFinished from a single goroutine (CU4 serial-dispatch
41	// contract); the sink translates each event into a tea.Msg, enqueues it on a
42	// bounded internal queue, and a pump goroutine forwards it via Program.Send —
43	// so only the pump can ever block on a stalled Bubble Tea loop, never the
44	// orchestrator.
45	//
46	// Cancellation: cancel is the same context.CancelFunc that controls the
47	// orchestrator's run context. The first KeyCtrlC in the dashboard fires this
48	// function (guarded by a sync.Once in the model) and switches the dashboard
49	// to a "Cancelling agents..." indicator while agents drain; a second KeyCtrlC
50	// force-quits without waiting. Out-of-TUI SIGINT routes through the cobra
51	// root's context, which cancels the same function — no parallel signal.Notify
52	// goroutine is needed here.
53	type TUISink struct {
54		program teaRunner
55	
56		mu       sync.Mutex
57		started  bool
58		finished bool
59		dropped  int
60	
61		msgs     chan tea.Msg  // bounded dispatch queue drained by the pump
62		done     chan struct{} // closed when the tea.Program exits
63		pumpDone chan struct{} // closed when the pump goroutine exits
64	}
65	
66	// Compile-time interface check.
67	var _ reviewtypes.Sink = (*TUISink)(nil)
68	
69	var tuiPostRunCompleteGrace = 2 * time.Second
70	
71	// NewTUISink creates a TUISink wired to cancel for Ctrl+C handling. agents is
72	// the ordered list of agent names that will run; the dashboard pre-renders one
73	// row per agent so the user sees the full run shape from the first frame.
74	// output is the writer the Bubble Tea program renders into (typically
75	// cmd.OutOrStdout()). input is the reader Bubble Tea reads keypresses from
76	// (typically os.Stdin in production); tests must pass a non-TTY reader (e.g.
77	// bytes.NewReader(nil)) so Bubble Tea does not put the inherited terminal
78	// into raw mode and corrupt sibling test output.
79	//
80	// tea.WithoutSignalHandler keeps SIGINT routing on the cobra root's existing
81	// handler (which cancels the run context), so the TUI's KeyCtrlC path and the
82	// OS signal path share a single cancel function with no race.
83	func NewTUISink(agents []string, cancel context.CancelFunc, output io.Writer, input io.Reader) *TUISink {
84		model := newReviewTUIModel(agents, cancel)
85		if measureTerminal := terminalMeasurer(output); measureTerminal != nil {
86			if width, height, ok := measureTerminal(); ok {
87				model.termWidth = width
88				model.termHeight = height
89			}
90		}
91		prog := tea.NewProgram(
92			model,
93			tea.WithOutput(output),
94			tea.WithInput(input),
95			tea.WithoutSignalHandler(), // SIGINT handled by cobra root; KeyCtrlC calls cancel directly
96		)
97		return newTUISinkWithProgram(prog)
98	}

100	// newTUISinkWithProgram wires a TUISink around any teaRunner; tests inject
101	// fakes with stalled or recording Send implementations.
102	func newTUISinkWithProgram(prog teaRunner) *TUISink {
103		return &TUISink{
104			program:  prog,
105			msgs:     make(chan tea.Msg, tuiSinkQueueCap),
106			done:     make(chan struct{}),
107			pumpDone: make(chan struct{}),
108		}
109	}

111	type fdWriter interface {
112		Fd() uintptr
113	}
114	
115	func terminalMeasurer(output io.Writer) func() (int, int, bool) {
116		f, ok := output.(fdWriter)
117		if !ok {
118			return nil
119		}
120		return func() (int, int, bool) {
121			width, height, err := term.GetSize(int(f.Fd())) //nolint:gosec // fd values fit in int on supported platforms
122			if err != nil || width <= 0 || height <= 0 {
123				return 0, 0, false
124			}
125			return width, height, true
126		}
127	}
128	
129	// Start spawns the Bubble Tea program in its own goroutine. Must be called
130	// before any AgentEvent calls. Subsequent calls are no-ops.
131	func (s *TUISink) Start() {
132		s.mu.Lock()
133		if s.started {
134			s.mu.Unlock()
135			return
136		}
137		s.started = true
138		s.mu.Unlock()
139	
140		go func() {
141			defer close(s.done)
142			if _, err := s.program.Run(); err != nil {
143				// Bubble Tea program errors are non-actionable in a background
144				// goroutine (e.g., terminal resize race on exit). Log nothing —
145				// the run result is available via RunSummary and the sink's
146				// finished state. Swallowing is intentional.
147				_ = err
148			}
149		}()

151		// Pump: the only goroutine allowed to block on Program.Send. When the
152		// program exits (done closes), a blocked Send unblocks via the program's
153		// context and the pump drains out.
154		go func() {
155			defer close(s.pumpDone)
156			for {
157				select {
158				case <-s.done:
159					return
160				case msg := <-s.msgs:
161					s.program.Send(msg)
162				}
163			}
164		}()
165	}
166	
167	// Wait blocks until the Bubble Tea program exits. Safe to call after Start.
168	// If Start was never called, Wait returns immediately.
169	func (s *TUISink) Wait() {
170		s.mu.Lock()
171		started := s.started
172		s.mu.Unlock()
173		if !started {
174			return
175		}
176		<-s.done
177	}
178	
179	// AgentEvent (Sink interface): translate ev into a tea.Msg and enqueue it for
180	// the pump. NEVER blocks: display events beyond the queue cap are dropped and
181	// counted rather than backpressuring the orchestrator's dispatch goroutine —
182	// see tuiSinkQueueCap for the incident this guards against.
183	func (s *TUISink) AgentEvent(agent string, ev reviewtypes.Event) {
184		s.mu.Lock()
185		ok := s.started && !s.finished
186		s.mu.Unlock()
187		if !ok {
188			return
189		}
190		select {
191		case s.msgs <- agentEventMsg{agent: agent, ev: ev}:
192		default:
193			s.mu.Lock()
194			s.dropped++

196		}
197	}

200	// summary, phase transitions, quit) with a bounded wait: worth briefly
201	// waiting out a transient jam, but a wedged TUI must not hold the run
202	// hostage — callers all have degradation paths (PostRunComplete falls back
203	// to Kill; a lost summary leaves the footer stale until quit).
204	func (s *TUISink) enqueueControl(msg tea.Msg) {
205		select {
206		case s.msgs <- msg:
207		case <-s.done:
208		case <-time.After(tuiPostRunCompleteGrace):
209			s.mu.Lock()

211			s.mu.Unlock()
212		}
213	}

216	// queue. Zero in any healthy run.

218		s.mu.Lock()

221	}

git add -A && git commit -m "fix(review): TUI sink must never backpressure the orchestrator

During a live full-crew dogfood run (2026-07-07, run 6), the parent
entire process wedged mid-run: the TUI stopped rendering (elapsed froze
at 11m58s, spinner ticks dead), the armed --timeout 20m never surfaced,
no judge ran, and the process had to be killed externally 15 minutes
later. The mechanism is structural: Program.Send is an unbuffered
BLOCKING send, and TUISink called it directly from the orchestrator's
serial dispatch goroutine — so any stall in the Bubble Tea Update/render
pipeline freezes sink dispatch, the bounded fanIn drain loop, the
forwarding goroutines, the stdout parsers, and reviewer-timeout event
handling with it. (The stall's own trigger was not reproduced in three
targeted shim experiments; this closes the amplification path that
turned a display stall into a full orchestrator freeze.)

TUISink now enqueues onto a bounded internal queue drained by a pump
goroutine — the only goroutine allowed to block on Send. Display events
(AgentEvent) never block: overflow beyond the 4096-message cap is
dropped and counted. Rare control messages (run summary, phase
transitions, quit) use a bounded wait, and PostRunComplete keeps its
Kill fallback, so a wedged TUI degrades to lost frames and a stale
footer instead of a hung run. Order is preserved through the single
queue for a healthy program.

Tests inject a deterministically wedged teaRunner: AgentEvent must
complete 3x the queue cap without blocking, control messages must
return within their bounded wait, and a recording runner pins FIFO
delivery.

gh pr create --base main --title "fix(review): TUI sink must never backpressure the orchestrator" --body "During a live full-crew dogfood run (2026-07-07), the parent \`entire review\` process wedged mid-run: the TUI stopped rendering (elapsed frozen at 11m58s, spinner ticks dead), an armed \`--timeout 20m\` never surfaced, no judge ran, and the process had to be killed externally 15 minutes later.

## Mechanism (proven)

\`Program.Send\` is an **unbuffered blocking send**, and \`TUISink\` called it directly from the orchestrator's serial dispatch goroutine. Any stall in the Bubble Tea Update/render pipeline therefore freezes, in order: sink dispatch → the bounded \`fanIn\` drain loop → the per-agent forwarding goroutines → the stdout parsers → reviewer-timeout event handling. Ticks are self-re-arming and commands run in independent goroutines, so a frozen elapsed counter is itself proof the Update loop was blocked. (The stall's own trigger was not reproduced across three targeted shim experiments — single-agent linger, multi-agent linger + burst, pre-fix tailer backlog — all of which enforced timeouts exactly; this PR closes the amplification path that turns *any* display stall into a full orchestrator freeze.)

## Change

- \`TUISink\` gains a bounded internal queue (4096) drained by a pump goroutine — the only goroutine allowed to block on \`Send\`.
- \`AgentEvent\` never blocks: overflow is dropped and counted (\`droppedCount\`), zero drops in any healthy run.
- Control messages (\`RunFinished\`, \`FinalPhase*\`, \`PostRunComplete\`) use a bounded wait; \`PostRunComplete\` keeps its existing Kill fallback. A wedged TUI now degrades to lost frames and a stale footer instead of a hung run with an unenforced timeout.
- FIFO order preserved through the single queue; \`teaRunner\` interface extracted so tests can inject a deterministically wedged program.

## Verification

- New tests: \`AgentEvent\` completes 3× the queue cap against a wedged program without blocking; control messages return within their bounded wait; a recording runner pins FIFO delivery. All \`-race\` clean.
- Full unit suite green (7,693), lint clean.
